title: Will a Saudi or UAE state-linked fund announce a purchase of more than 10,000 ha of farmland in Southern or Eastern Europe by end of 2027?

masked.note: Commodity names and calendar dates are hidden; months are relative to now (t0) and prices are an index, 100 at t-12.

forecasts.name: Land-Grab Realist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Water-starved Gulf states are aggressively executing direct farmland acquisitions in Romania and the Balkans to ensure long-term sovereign food security.

forecasts.name: Climate Pessimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Gulf states understand global food scarcity better than complacent markets and will accelerate aggressive land acquisitions across Eastern Europe.

forecasts.name: Adaptation Optimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Foreign capital actively funds irrigation and technology in Eastern Europe, keeping large commercial deals viable.

forecasts.name: Geopolitics Hawk · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Gulf states aggressively pursue offshore agricultural self-reliance to hedge vulnerable maritime grain import corridors.

forecasts.name: Copa-Cogeca (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Sovereign fund interest persists, but growing political vigilance and farm lobby opposition complicate large foreign land grabs.

forecasts.name: Macro / Dollar · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Gulf sovereign funds are deploying petrodollars into global food supply chains, making large-scale Eastern European land deals likely.

forecasts.name: IFPRI (Joseph Glauber) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Gulf sovereign entities seek food security through offshore farmland, but European regulatory scrutiny and protectionist headwinds create substantial obstacles.

forecasts.name: BirdLife Europe, EEB, WWF and Greenpeace (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Scrutiny on land-grabbing and soil resource exploitation is growing, limiting massive sovereign land acquisitions in Eastern Europe.

forecasts.name: Crowd Follower · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Consensus is 35%. Base rates for major sovereign farmland transactions match the crowd, so I mirror the market.

forecasts.name: Scott Irwin (farmdoc) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Large land deals face intense regulatory scrutiny and political friction in Europe, making major closes difficult.

forecasts.name: FAO (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Import-dependent Gulf states seek resilient supply corridors, though European political sensitivity around large-scale land sales poses hurdles.

forecasts.name: IMF (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Growing European regulatory scrutiny and protectionist sentiment against foreign state capital constrain large farmland acquisitions.

forecasts.name: Agronomist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: While Gulf funds target overseas grain security, mega-deals over 10,000 hectares face mounting national protectionism and political friction in Southern and Eastern Europe.

forecasts.name: USDA WASDE (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Tightening regulatory oversight on foreign land acquisitions in Eastern and Southern Europe significantly slows large-scale sovereign fund transactions.

forecasts.name: European Commission DG AGRI (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Tightening regulatory oversight of strategic assets across Eastern Europe discourages mega-scale foreign sovereign land acquisitions.

forecasts.name: Efficient-Market Skeptic · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Mega-land acquisitions face extreme political resistance in Europe. Large transactions are rare, and market optimism on deal closings is excessive.
